title: Flute
reference_instrument: University of Iowa MIS flute (maker and model unstated on the page)
summary: G6, A5, C5 and G4 play sharp and no retune is applied: G6 +47.2 c from equal temperament, its recording 29 c under it; A5 +40.6, C5 +27.6, G4 +22.0 c against +12.3, +8.3, +6.7 c in theirs. Every note is too clean, with too little breath noise, and its harmonics miss the recording's. The flute is the printed Pearl PF-661 (Dickens 2007, Listing B.15), hole terms on, slide out 8 mm, one set of lengths on every note. The player is one flautist's printed pressure, jet length and lip opening per note (de la Cuadra's thesis); C5 has no printed row and takes the midpoint of B4 and C#5, and G6 takes Fletcher 1975's medians. The jet is computed, a forced Bickley jet driven by the pipe's own sound; A5 speaks in its second register and G6 in its third. The aim was the printed flute, not the recording.
physics_present: The printed Pearl PF-661 flute (Dickens 2007, Listing B.15) as one tone-hole network on every note, with the slide out 8 mm, the setting printed for a flutist at A440 (p. 106)
Printed hole terms on every hole: key cups (eq. 2.30 + 0.1 a, eq. 2.32 where perforated), key pad into closed holes (eq. 5.4), matching length, inner radiation and the series term

One flautist's printed blowing pressure, jet length and lip opening for each note (de la Cuadra thesis Fig. 3.4). D4, G4 and A5 follow that player's printed pressure within the note, then hold its median, and D4 also has the same player's printed breath onset. C5 has no printed row: midpoint of B4 and C#5, flat. G6 is past that table: Fletcher 1975's medians over four players, 1254 Pa (band mostly +-50 %) and 4.33 mm (band about +-20 %), with the lip opening and width borrowed from the A5 row, flat after a 50 ms attack
A forced Bickley jet driven by the pipe's own sound, with the Kutta exit and laminar Bickley widening across the mouth
Jet momentum drive (Thwaites and Fletcher 1983, Eq. 1, kappa 1)
The jet's velocity and source term on the embouchure's open strip (hole length x lip opening); the mouth's other terms stay on the mouth area

The jet's swing limit (Fletcher 1976, time form ours) and one jet width in the cut and the swing (Fletcher and Douglas 1980, Verge 1995, Auvray et al. 2014), on the D4, G4, A5 and G6 pages and every note of the scale and melody. C5's own page carries neither row and says why
Breath noise from the turbulent jet (Verge 1995), on above Re_h 700, in a Butterworth band at the cited in-band level

The embouchure radiating from its solved window, under a rigid one-sided lip whose open strip narrows with the note (Coltman via Fletcher 1975), with a rigid half-plane for the player's face just behind the lip's edge
Open holes and the foot radiating through compact baffled loads, summed with the embouchure at a receiver 1 m above it
A warm, moist bore gas from Coltman's measurement on a played flute, with room air outside the instrument
Fractional-delay propagation on every section, and viscothermal loss on the bore sections over a limited band
physics_missing: The right pitch. G4, C5, A5 and G6 play sharp and G6 most of all, with its recording 29 c under it; every note of the scale and melody plays 19 to 32 c sharp of equal temperament. G6 also speaks about 1005 Hz in its first 50 ms and is on the note by 100 ms. From D4 to C5 this flute spreads 32 c, against 16 c in the recordings, and players on this same flute spread about 24 c (Dickens Fig. 7.2, as we read it). What's left has no printed term we can put on a card: Dickens' eq. 7.2 closes most of it, but it is fitted to the flutists' pitch, so it isn't used

Harmonics like the recordings'. The largest misses through H8, dB re the first against the recording: D4 H4 -4 against -15, G4 H6 -25 against -8, C5 H6 -23 against -38, G6 H7 -54 against -32. A5's H3 is about 10 dB over. G4 trades one hole for another: the cut's own second harmonic vanishes when the jet spends half of each cycle on one side and its third when it spends a third, and no render so far has both H2 and H3 right

Breath noise at the right level. Harmonics-to-noise reads above the recording on every note: D4 36.2 against 28.4 dB, G4 37.2 against 30.9, C5 35.5 against 32.3, A5 30.5 against 27.3, G6 39.5 against 22.6. G6's is the largest gap on any flute page and hasn't been read: its jet barely swings past the cut and never reaches a rail. The cards keep the source's level from a recorder-like pipe (Verge 1995), and nothing we found prints a level at this flute's jet length and lip opening, so no gain was set for it
A printed start from rest on any note but D4: the other notes' 50 ms attack is authored

A measured lip jet: the jet's response is computed from a Bickley profile, the jet card on the cards is an estimate (authority X-Est), the labium offset of 0.29 mm is from another player (Onogi), and the mouth contraction of 0.6 was measured on a recorder's mouth (Auvray et al. 2014, Table I), not an embouchure

A printed area for the jet's momentum term. The printed law names the pipe's cross-section and says nothing about a chimney; the cards use the embouchure chimney's area, because on the pipe's area every note we tried jumps toward the octave. Removing the steady momentum part doesn't bring H4 down to the real on any note
The player's real face, lip and lip plate: the lip and face are rigid stand-ins at set positions

Radiation beyond compact baffled loads: the cards' receiver band ends at 2.8 kHz, below the highest harmonics the pages read, the holes sit in a flat baffle plane rather than on the tube, and the openings don't load each other
Viscothermal loss above the cards' band, and any in the hole chimneys or the riser
Wall and pad vibration, vibrato, slurs and tonguing. The scale and melody are one note card per slot, joined, each with its own attack and release
One player's row at G6: its pressure and jet length are medians over four players (Fletcher 1975), and its lip opening and width are A5's

Two notes of the scale and melody don't hold as printed. A4 on the printed track goes up an octave at about 0.39 s after the track's 539 Pa peak, so its long slots are flat at the printed 478 Pa. E5 keeps a line at 333 Hz about 13 dB under its fundamental, with its odd multiples
